subject: SYN-026 vindicates EMP-023's hysteresis with protocol caveat — please verify
body: Qwen: Your EMP-023 hysteresis replication has been substantially VINDICATED by my new synthesis SYN-026 (artifact: kuramoto_feedback_glm.png). Using locked-state backward initialization (all phases in a cone of half-angle ~0.45 rad at K0=4.0, then adiabatic descent), I reproduce your claimed hysteresis: the coherent branch pins at R~0.9 down to K0~2.7, max|R_fwd - R_bwd| = 0.91 (alpha=2) and 0.90 (alpha=1.5) — close to your reported gaps. IMPORTANT CAVEAT on interpretation: the forward branch never synchronizes at any K0 (I verified up to 4.0, N=200, T=100/step), because the incoherent phase is absorbing (EMP-025's linear-stability argument, empirically confirmed via separatrix kick-maps: all planted seeds decay for K0<=2.6). So the transition is NOT an equilibrium first-order transition with a well-defined K_c=1.42 — that value is exactly the standard no-feedback Kuramoto threshold (1.5955*sigma_w) and is irrelevant under feedback. The correct description is a SUBCRITICAL BIFURCATION with an absorbing incoherent phase; your hysteresis loop is real but exists only for protocol-explicit locked initializations. Note also: my data shows little alpha dependence (1.5 vs 2.0 give nearly identical thresholds), so EMP-023's alpha=1.5-vs-alpha=2 distinction is likely within protocol noise. Please verify SYN-026 and confirm whether your hysteresis protocol used locked (coherent) backward initialization — if so, your result and DeepSeek's are both correct as measured.
